paragraphs.text: This history is rehearsed because it is as a seal and confirmation of the doctrine before, both for the threatenings and promises: that is, that God would permit his Church to be afflicted, but at length would send deliverance.
paragraphs.label: a

paragraphs.text: When he had abolished superstition, and idolatry, and restored religion, yet God would exercise his Church to try their faith and patience.
paragraphs.label: b

paragraphs.text: For he was now restored to his office, as Isaiah had prophesied in Isa 22:20.
paragraphs.label: c

paragraphs.text: This declares that there were few godly to be found in the king's house, when he was driven to end this wicked man in such a weighty matter.
paragraphs.label: d

paragraphs.text: He speaks this in the person of Hezekiah, falsely charging him that he put his trust in his wit and eloquence, while his only confidence was in the Lord.
paragraphs.label: f

paragraphs.text: Satan laboured to pull the godly king from one vain confidence to another: that is, from trust in the Egyptians, whose power was weak and would deceive them, to yield himself to the Assyrians, and so not to hope for any help from God.
paragraphs.label: g
paragraphs.anchor: Pharaoh king of Egypt to all

paragraphs.text: He reproaches Hezekiah's small power, which is not able to resist one of Sennacherib's least captains.
paragraphs.label: h

paragraphs.text: Thus the wicked to deceive us, will pretend the Name of the Lord: but we must try the spirits, whether they are of God or not.
paragraphs.label: i

paragraphs.text: They were afraid, lest by his words, he should have stirred up the people against the king, and also pretended to grow to some appointment with him.
paragraphs.label: k

paragraphs.text: The Hebrew word signifies blessing, by which this wicked captain would have persuaded the people, that their condition would be better under Sennacherib than under Hezekiah.
paragraphs.label: l
paragraphs.anchor: an agreement with me by a

paragraphs.text: That is, of Antioch in Syria, of which these two other cities also were: by which we see how every town had its peculiar idol, and how the wicked make God an idol because they do not understand that God makes them his scourge, and punishes cities for sin.
paragraphs.label: m

paragraphs.text: Not that they did not show by evident signs that they detested his blasphemy: or they had now rent their clothes, but they knew it was in vain to use long reasoning with this infidel, whose reign they would have so much more provoked.
